title: Open-extended injectives are proper-direct-image acyclic on pro-etale sites
statement:
Let $p:B\to D$ and $r:C\to E$ be proper morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $k:C\hookrightarrow B$ and $i:E\hookrightarrow D$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with $p\circ k=i\circ r$. The square is not required to be cartesian. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and use constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every injective object $J$ of $\operatorname{Mod}(A_C)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], its extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero] is $p_*$-acyclic:
$$R^q p_*(k_!J)=0\qquad(q>0).$$
Here $R^qp_*$ means $\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(-[0]))$ for the ordinary uncompleted derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. There is no etale-origin hypothesis on $J$.

source.place: Clause (b), compactification independence: agent-extracted injective-acyclicity obligation for the pro-etale proper/open argument. proof.text: Form the fibre product $V=B\times_D E$ with projections $b:V\to B$ and $s:V\to E$. Base change preserves proper morphisms, so $s$ is proper, while base change of the open immersion $i$ makes $b$ an open immersion. The equation $pk=ir$ gives a unique map $t=(k,r):C\to V$ with $b t=k$ and $s t=r$. Since $k$ is an open immersion and $b$ identifies $V$ with the open $p^{-1}(E)$ in $B$, the map $t$ is an open immersion. The morphism $s$ is separated (proper), and $r=s t$ is proper; hence $t$ is proper by properness over a separated target. A proper immersion is a closed immersion, so $t(C)$ is both open and closed in $V$.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, case (b), fibre-product and clopen-component reduction; morphisms.tex Tags 01W4 and 01W6

proof.text: On the clopen decomposition $V=t(C)\amalg(V\setminus t(C))$, extension by zero identifies a module sheaf on $C$ with the pair consisting of that sheaf on the first component and the zero sheaf on the second. This follows by the pro-etale open-closed exact sequence and the open-extension adjunction, evaluated on the two components. Consequently $t_!J$ is injective: for a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$ and a map $M\to t_!J$, restrict to $C$, extend the resulting map to $N|_C$ using injectivity of $J$, and glue it with the zero map on the complementary clopen component. The glued map is the required lift. The same componentwise description identifies $t_!J$ with $t_*J$; no exactness of a general open direct image is being used.

source.place: Tag 09AH, open-closed exact sequence, together with the componentwise lifting argument for a clopen immersion

proof.text: Put $F=k_!J$ and $M=Rp_*(F[0])$. Apply the derived open-restriction isomorphism to the Cartesian square with source open $b:V\hookrightarrow B$ and base open $i:E\hookrightarrow D$. It gives $i^*M\cong Rs_*(b^*F[0])$. The extension-by-zero base-change isomorphism identifies $b^*k_!J$ with $t_!J$: the pullback $C\times_BV$ is $C$, since $k$ factors through $V$. Consequently $i^*M\cong Rs_*(t_*J[0])$. By step 2 this input is injective. The module category is Grothendieck by the resolution-existence statement, hence has enough injectives by the cited Grothendieck theorem. The one-term complex $t_*J[0]$ is a bounded-below complex of injectives, hence K-injective by the bounded-below representative theorem, so the defined $Rs_*$ is computed on it termwise; the right-derived injective computation likewise makes the right side $s_*t_*J$ concentrated in degree zero. Exactness of the identified-coefficient inverse image therefore gives $i^*R^qp_*F=0$ for $q>0$. This proves only the restriction to $E$; it makes no identification of $M$ with an open direct image.

proof.text: Fix $q>0$ and write $G=R^qp_*F$. To prove $G=0$ it suffices to show it vanishes locally on every site object, by the sheaf equalizer axiom. First cover such an object by affine opens. For an affine object $Q_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0\to D$, the w-contractible-ring extension gives a one-member pro-etale cover $Q=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Q_0$ with every faithfully flat weakly etale $R$-algebra admitting a retraction. Choose its cardinal parameter large enough to contain $R_0$, in the fixed site universes. Composition of weakly etale maps makes $Q\to D$ a site object. It is enough to prove $G(Q)=0$ for each such cover. The pullback $E_Q=E\times_DQ$ is a quasi-compact open of $Q$. Since principal opens form a basis, quasi-compactness supplies finitely many $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in R$ with $E_Q=\bigcup_aD(f_a)$; the empty list is permitted. Put $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and $Z_Q=\operatorname{Spec}(R/I)$.

source.place: Proposition 0983, proposition-find-w-contractible, with the size-controlled node cited; affine principal-open refinement is the definition of the affine topology and quasi-compactness.

proof.text: Let $S=\{s\in R:s\bmod I\in(R/I)^\times\}$ and $Q^\sim=\operatorname{Spec}(S^{-1}R)$. The closed-localization lemma gives a pro-etale cover of $Q$ consisting of the $D(f_a)$ and $Q^\sim$. Every point of $Q^\sim$ specializes to $Z^\sim=Q^\sim\times_Q Z_Q$, and $S^{-1}R$ has the same ring-retraction property as $R$. Since the $D(f_a)$ factor through $E$, step 3 gives $G(D(f_a))=0$. It remains to show $G(Q^\sim)=0$. The localization is a site object over $D$ by composition of weakly etale maps. The ring-to-site weak-contractibility statement, followed by exact module evaluation, shows evaluation on $Q^\sim$ preserves homology of complexes of constant-$A$ module sheaves on $D$.

source.place: Tags 096V (lemma-localization), 0987 (lemma-localization-w-contractible), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open, displayed localization cover), 098H (lemma-w-contractible-is-weakly-contractible); sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0946 (lemma-w-contractible).

proof.text:
Put $P=B\times_DQ^\sim$, $U=C\times_DQ^\sim$, $E^\sim=E\times_DQ^\sim$, and let $p^\sim:P\to Q^\sim$ and $k^\sim:U\hookrightarrow P$ be the projections. Properness and quasi-compact openness are preserved by base change. The map $U\hookrightarrow P\times_{Q^\sim}E^\sim$ is the base change of the clopen map $t$ of step 1, hence is clopen: its image is the inverse image of the clopen subset $t(C)$, and base change preserves its open-immersion identification. The projection $U\to C$ is weakly etale, so the restriction $J^\sim$ of $J$ is injective. Extension-by-zero base change gives $F|_P\cong k^\sim_!J^\sim$. Choose a bounded-below injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $F[0]$; it exists by the Grothendieck property, the enough-injectives theorem, and the bounded-below representative theorem. It computes $Rp_*F$. Exact evaluation from step 5 gives
$$G(Q^\sim)=H^q((p_*I^\bullet)(Q^\sim))=H^q(I^\bullet(P))=H^q(P_{\mathrm{proet}},k^\sim_!J^\sim).$$
The middle equality is the direct-image section formula. For the last equality, restriction along the weakly etale projection $P\to B$ is exact and preserves injectives, so $I^\bullet|_P$ computes derived global sections of $F|_P$. This resolves $F$ on $B$, not $J$ on $C$, and assumes no acyclicity of $k_!J$.

source.place: Tags 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic) and 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived); weakly-etale localization used in proetale.tex Tag 09AE (definition-extension-zero), via sites.tex Section 00XZ and sites-modules.tex Section 03DH; extension-by-zero base change is the cited pro-etale statement. Explicit evaluation calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-proetale-proper-boundary-cohomology] to $Q^\sim$, its closed subscheme $Z^\sim$, its quasi-compact open complement $E^\sim$, the proper map $p^\sim$, and the clopen open $U\subset P\times_{Q^\sim}E^\sim$. Step 5 verifies both the ring-retraction and specialization hypotheses; step 6 verifies properness, quasi-compactness of $k^\sim$, and injectivity of $J^\sim$. It gives $H^q(P_{\mathrm{proet}},k^\sim_!J^\sim)=0$, so $G(Q^\sim)=0$. On the cover of step 5 every restriction of a section of $G(Q)$ is now zero. Separatedness of $G$ gives $G(Q)=0$. The covers in step 4 then give $G=0$ on every site object. This proves $R^qp_*(k_!J)=0$ for all $q>0$. The new cited statement is precisely the boundary-cohomology input; neither degree-zero specialization vanishing nor the etale Tag 0F7B is used as its proof.
